title: Nuxt.js Small Examples
description: Use these small Nuxt.js examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Show the current page
examples.description: NuxtPage is the place where Nuxt displays the page chosen by the address.
examples.output: The home route shows the index page through NuxtPage.

examples.title: Add a file route
examples.description: A Vue file in pages becomes a route. index.vue is the home page, while books.vue makes /books.
examples.output: The /books route shows the book list.

examples.title: Navigate with NuxtLink
examples.description: NuxtLink provides a normal link meaning while letting Nuxt handle local route navigation.
examples.output: The link opens the existing /books route.

examples.title: Share a layout
examples.description: A layout wraps pages with shared content.
examples.output: Pages appear between the shared header and footer.

examples.title: Reuse a component
examples.description: Nuxt can auto-import components from its components folder.
examples.output: The books page shows the auto-imported BookCard with its title.

examples.title: Set the page title
examples.description: useSeoMeta describes title and description values for a page.
examples.output: The browser tab and generated page metadata use the supplied title and description.

examples.title: Share state with a key
examples.description: useState creates state that Nuxt can share safely within one app visit.
examples.output: The button updates the shared value named books-read.

examples.title: Load a local JSON file
examples.description: useFetch can load data and give the page loading and error state.
examples.output: With the real JSON file present, the page shows Moon Trip. A failure has its own message.

examples.title: Read a route value
examples.description: A bracketed page file captures part of an address.
examples.output: The route /books/moon-trip displays Book: moon-trip. Static generation must be told which such routes to build.

examples.title: Run browser-only work after mount
examples.description: Some APIs exist only in the browser. onMounted runs after the component is mounted there, so it can safely read browser-only objects.
examples.output: The page begins with Checking and then shows the browser width after mounting.

examples.title: Keep a public setting public
examples.description: Runtime config separates public settings from server-only settings.
examples.output: A component can read the public club name. It is ordinary visible configuration, not a secret.

examples.title: Generate static pages
examples.description: Nuxt can build a site as static files. List dynamic routes that cannot be found by following ordinary page links.
examples.output: The output contains generated pages and assets for the listed routes and the pages found by the generator.
